problem.text: A box contains $5$ chips, numbered $1$, $2$, $3$, $4$, and $5$. Chips are drawn randomly one at a time without replacement until the sum of the values drawn exceeds $4$. What is the probability that $3$ draws are required?

steps.title: Where to start: what must the first two chips do?
steps.body: Needing exactly $3$ draws means the sum is still at most $4$ after two chips, and goes above $4$ after the third. So the question is really about the first two chips. Check whether the third chip could ever fail to push the sum above $4$.

your_turn.prompt: Suppose the first two chips add to at most $4$. Can the sum still be at most $4$ after the third chip?
your_turn.answer: No. Any three different chips add to at least $1 + 2 + 3 = 6$, which is more than $4$.

steps.title: List the small pairs
steps.body: So $3$ draws are needed exactly when the first two chips add to $4$ or less. The chips are all different, so there are only a few pairs of chips small enough.

your_turn.prompt: Which pairs of chips add to at most $4$?
your_turn.answer: $\{1,2\}$ (sum $3$) and $\{1,3\}$ (sum $4$). Any pair without chip $1$ adds to at least $2 + 3 = 5$.

steps.title: Count good and total outcomes the same way
steps.body: You can count the first two chips as an unordered pair or as an ordered pair (first chip, second chip). Either works, but the good outcomes and all outcomes must be counted the same way. Careful: if you list the good pairs without order but count all outcomes with order, you get an answer that is too small.

your_turn.prompt: How many ordered pairs (first chip, second chip) are good?

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body:
Without order, the first two chips form one of $\binom{5}{2} = 10$ equally likely pairs, and $2$ of them are good. With order, there are $5 \cdot 4 = 20$ outcomes, and $4$ are good. Both give the same result.
$$\frac{2}{10} = \frac{4}{20} = \frac{1}{5}$$
The answer is **(D)** $\frac{1}{5}$.

wrong_choices.B: $\frac{1}{10}$ comes from counting the $2$ good pairs without order but dividing by the $20$ ordered outcomes. Count both the same way: $\frac{4}{20}$ or $\frac{2}{10}$.

verification.verifier_notes: Passed adversarial verifier on first review.
